points.t: Child with **fever, sore throat** and a fine **rough ‘sandpaper’ rash** from neck and chest, folds accentuated, **strawberry tongue**.
**Phenoxymethylpenicillin 10 days** (clarithromycin if allergic); off school until **24 h of antibiotics**; notify UKHSA.
**Invasive GAS**; Kawasaki disease and toxic shock as differentials.

cause.lead: A throat infection whose toxin paints the skin.
points: Usually after **strep pharyngitis / tonsillitis**, occasionally a skin or wound source.
Droplets and contact; incubation **2–5 days**; winter–spring peaks; UK surges (2022–23 with more iGAS).
**SpeA/B/C superantigens** cause the rash and enanthem; immunity is toxin-specific, so repeat episodes happen.

features.lead: Throat first, then a rash you can feel.
points: Abrupt **fever, sore throat**, tender nodes, headache, vomiting, abdominal pain.
After 12–48 h: **fine pinhead ‘sandpaper’ erythema** from neck / chest; blanches; **Pastia lines** in folds.
**Flushed cheeks with circumoral pallor**; on darker skin the rash may be hard to see but **feels rough**.
**White strawberry tongue** (day 1–2) → **red strawberry tongue** (day 3–5); palatal petechiae.
Rash fades in ~1 week, then **peeling** of fingertips, toes, groin.

visuals.caption: Scarlet fever: flushed cheeks with a pale ring around the mouth, a fine pinpoint rash on neck and chest, and a red strawberry tongue.

points: Culture or rapid antigen if uncertain or outbreaks.
FBC, CRP, blood cultures; ASO retrospectively.

cards.name: Kawasaki disease
cards.clue: **Fever ≥ 5 days**, conjunctivitis, red cracked lips, swollen then peeling hands / feet; < 5 years: urgent paediatrics.

cards.name: SSSS
cards.clue: Tender erythema, flaccid blisters, Nikolsky +, no tonsillitis.

cards.name: Viral exanthems
cards.clue: Measles (coryza, cough, Koplik), slapped cheek; no sandpaper texture.

manage.lead: Treat to speed recovery and cut spread (UKHSA / CKS).

points: Off school / nursery / work **until 24 h after starting antibiotics**; untreated cases infectious ~2–3 weeks.

rx.dose: BNF age-banded; e.g. ≥ 12 years 500 mg four times daily (or 1 g twice daily per local guidance)

points: **Clarithromycin** (5 days) or azithromycin per BNF; **amoxicillin** 10 days if liquid palatability or supply is an issue.

limits.t: Higher iGAS risk: lower threshold for review.
In writing, for iGAS; dark urine or swelling 1–3 weeks later.

items.t: Rapid deterioration, severe pain, spreading skin infection, breathing difficulty, sepsis: **invasive GAS**.
Fever ≥ 5 days with red eyes, red lips, swollen hands / feet: consider **Kawasaki disease**.
Dark urine or swelling 1–3 weeks later: check urine (post-strep nephritis).

pearls.t: Sandpaper rash + sore throat + strawberry tongue + circumoral pallor = scarlet fever until proven otherwise.
On darker skin rely on **texture and the tongue**.
Strawberry tongue isn’t specific: ≥ 5 days’ fever needs Kawasaki excluded.
Warn that fingers and toes may peel 1–2 weeks later.

quiz.q: When can the child return to school?
Strawberry tongue and 6 days of fever with conjunctivitis?
quiz.a: Consider Kawasaki disease: urgent paediatric referral.
